Alex.confusing: How hugs interact with visitor-based roles like Turkey and Eagle was hard to reason about, and so was whether dead players' throws count. Both shaped what the table could deduce.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when Ellis's Owl visitor list let the table catch Drew the Mouser and Blair the Floofer, and my 20-point stake banked.
Alex.change: I'd make the Wink's effect more visible or traceable. Now a wink mostly reads as noise, and the Meowfia hold a very strong hidden tool.
Alex.regret: In round 2, as Meowfia, I claimed Eagle and then accused Drew, and I threw at him. Finley was my partner and got eggsecuted, and I only threw a Wild, so I scored little. I should have stayed quieter. I also never used the Wink, so I'd use it on a loud accuser.

Blair.confusing: How a hug spreads was unclear: the rules say visitors to a Floofer get hugged, but it was hard to tell from dawn reports whether a hug came from visiting someone or being visited. Egg counts for Eagle and Tit visits also took some working out.
Blair.fun: In round 3, Blair's dead throw of three cards at Drew banked 29 points for the Farm side after Drew was eggsecuted, which was a big swing.
Blair.change: I would make dawn reports name who visited a player, or at least say whether a hug came from a visit, so claims about visits can be checked more easily.
Blair.regret: In round 1, as the Meowfia Floofer, I falsely claimed to be a Pigeon when Ellis had already named me, which made my story easy to catch. I would have stayed quiet or claimed a role I could defend.

Casey.confusing: How hugs and confusion interact with egg counts, e.g. whether a hugged Turkey or Owl still shows an egg change, made cross-checking claims hard.
Casey.fun: Catching Finley in round 2: her claim to have visited me didn't match my Kookaburra report, which showed no confusion. Seeing the whole table pile onto her was satisfying.
Casey.change: I'd add a clearer in-game summary of each role's expected egg effects, so players can check claims without redoing the math each time.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I jumped to Drew on his Mouser confession and Ellis's list without testing the other claims. It worked out, but I would stake fewer high cards when the evidence is thinner. Otherwise none.

Drew.confusing: How hugs interact with the claimed visits was hard to read: a hugged Owl gets no egg, but it was unclear whether a hug also blocks the visitor's own gain. Several players also misread who a hug or Turkey egg came from.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was a good read: Finley's Tit story shifted under questioning, and Casey caught the contradiction about whether Finley visited the Kookaburra.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since many claims were unverifiable and the table had to guess from egg counts alone.
Drew.regret: I used my Wink on Alex in round 1, a Farm player, which removed a claim and cost me the Wink later. I would have held it and checked the Floofer lead before spending it.

Ellis.confusing: How hugs interact with visits. I couldn't tell whether a hugged player's report was reliable, or whether a hug lands on the Floofer's target or also on visitors to the Floofer.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, when my Owl list of Floofer, Kookaburra and Mouser exposed both cats at once and Drew confessed Mouser. The table then piled on him.
Ellis.change: Let dawn reports give a bit more verifiable info, or show who threw how much earlier. Wink kills with no trace make the day feel less deducible.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I staked only two cards (a 9 and a Wild) on Finley and kept a 9. Once Casey caught Finley's lie, I should have thrown both 9s, since all the Farm throws banked anyway.

Finley.confusing: The Tit's egg rule was hard to track: I guessed Owl in round 3 and missed, but my dawn report only showed a Turkey egg, so I couldn't tell whether a correct guess would have paid out. Also, the hug mechanics (Floofer hugs both the visited player and any visitor) made the night logic hard to check.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when I was the Floofer and kept deflecting by hugging a Farm player and then arguing about the Owl's empty report, the table got tangled in its own accusations. Watching Casey and Ellis argue over the Kookaburra confusion check was also fun.
Finley.change: Make the dawn report show exactly which role effect produced each egg, so players can check claims like the Tit guess against the actual result.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I corrected my Tit claim after Ellis challenged it, which made me look shifty, and I threw my stake at Ellis instead of staying quiet. I would hold my claim steady and throw nothing at a Farm target unless the vote was close.
